analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (10.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 2.35% (reported as +235bps) to 7550, +10% YTD, with 423 S&P stocks closing higher. GS US desks saw a mix of short covering and long buying across Tech. Power Up America rose 6% and Memory rose 8%.
Kospi rose 5% on 10 Nov, with SK Hynix up 7% and Samsung up 5%. Nvidia fell 4% after a headline about Jensen Huang's personal affair, losing more than $150bn of market cap.
The desk notes CTA selling pressure against more buybacks. US 10-year yield is 4.88%, Brent $92, Gold $4,122 and Bitcoin $75k.
Market pricing is 84% for a Fed hike in December, ahead of US inflation data on 10 Nov. CoreWeave reports 10 Nov, with Cisco and Applied Materials on Thursday.
Oil eased after Trump said renewed US attacks on Iran were 'highly unlikely'.
GS Prime Brokerage: US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of total US net market value, in the 1st, 1st and 3rd percentiles on 1-year, 3-year and 5-year lookbacks.

GS recommends shorting its Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP, 43 stocks). Earnings and dividend yields look unattractive against fixed income, earnings revisions are rolling over and valuations are in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.

The US Senate advanced a bill to speed permit reviews for infrastructure projects by a 73-25 vote. It would shorten timelines for large energy projects and require data centers to pay for the energy they use.

GS US consumer outlook for 2027: consumer spending is forecast to grow 2.2%, near potential. Tax refunds and equity gains offset energy price drag in 2026, real income growth is expected to be more evenly distributed, and the 3.8% saving rate is not a concern.

AI infrastructure is 15% of the STOXX 600 versus 40% of the S&P 500. GS argues Europe's smaller AI exposure becomes an advantage as markets shift from spending to returns, and that earnings growth would be stronger in Europe if the AI earnings boom paused.

A call with the EUDCA Secretary General: European data center development is unaffected by US midterms, the market could more than double by the early 2030s, and power grids are the largest bottleneck. GS points to its European Power Basket (GSXEPOWR, 39 stocks).

GS views the Semis drawdown as overdone. 35 GW of 2027 deployments are largely in progress with low execution risk. NVDA and AVGO are at very attractive entry points, and AMAT and LRCX are particularly compelling.

A GS credit update says hyperscaler debt issuance equals 36% of GS equity research's 2026 Capex forecast, above the initial 33% expectation. This partly reflects pull-forward of planned 2027 supply, and GS sees scope for more front-loading.
GS lowered its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150/toz from $4,650 and its end-2027 forecast to $4,800/toz from $5,400, citing the Fed's hawkish shift and its effect on positioning.
States where Democrats are likely to further restrict data centers account for about 45% of planned US data center capacity.
Cited a16z data: GLP-1 households spend more on food than the average household, and dining out is slightly above the pre-GLP-1 baseline by the middle of the second year.
